lawyer:
For the Appellants ------ Mr. Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate, (Mr. Md. Ozair Farooq, Senior Advocate and Mr. Probir Neogi, Advocate with him) instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-record. 
For Respondent Nos.1-5: Mr. Kh. Mahbubuddin Ahmed, Senior Advocate, (Mr. M.I. Farooqui, Senior Advocate and Mr. Abdul Quayum, Senior Advocate with him) instructed by Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-record. 
For Respondent No.6-8: Not Represented.
parties:

Versus
Md. Balai Roy and others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, J.: This is a defendants' (defendant Nos.1 and 2) appeal, by leave, against the judgment of 23rd October, 2000 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 898 of 1995 making the Rule absolute upon reversing the judgment and decree of November 24, 1994 of the 2nd Court of Additional District Judge, Dhaka in Title Appeal No. 77 of 1993 setting aside the judgment and decree. of February 9, 1993 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, (now Joint District Judge), Dhaka passed in Title Suit No.396 of 1976 decreeing the same. The suit was filed on September 3, 1976.

2. The suit was filed seeking reliefs (a) title to the "property described in the schedule-A attached to the plaint, (b) a decree' for khas possession in respect of the property described in schedule-B which is part of the property described in schedule 'A' and (c) for declaration that the deed No.16157 dated %27.10.1969 in favour of Ali Ahmed Khandker and the deed No.16158 dated 27.10.1969 in favour of Wali Mohammad Siddiqui said to have been executed by Jatindra Mohan Roy @ Sachindra Mohan Roy as described in schedule 'C' are forged, nul and void, fabricated and the deeds 'executed and registered by Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui in favour of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 are illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff (the last relief Was inserted in pursuant to the order of the Court dated November 19, 1988 allowing prayer for amendment of the plaint). The application seeking amendment of the plaint was filed on July 10, 1988:

3. The suit was filed by the Respondent Nos.1-5's predecessor Jatindra Mohan Roy, who died during pendency of the suit, stating, inter alia, that he inherited the property described in schedule 'A' attached to the plaint (the property in question is of Municipal Holding No.62 Bama Charan Chakraborty Road, Dhaka) on the death of his father Krishna Chandra Karmaker, son of Haridas Karmaker to whom the land in suit belonged, that he owned and possessed the land upon mutating his name in the revenue record and in other official records and paid rent as well as the municipal holding taxes, that he let out portion of the suit property to the monthly tenants including the defendant No.3 (Respondent No.7), that defendant No.5 (Respondent No.8) being his relation has been enjoying a portion of the land in suit as licensee, that in the year 1968 when law and order situation in the locality deteriorated he left the area for the time being and could not take care of the property, that defendant Nos. and 2 having no right, title and interest since liberation of Bangladesh occupied the land described in schedule 'B' and when plaintiff asked them to vacate the land they disclosed that they have purchased the property in suit from one Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui who said to have purchased the property in suit from Jatindra Mohon Roy @ Sachindra Mohon Roy, although the land in suit was never transferred by the plaintiff to the said two persons by executing and registering any deed of sale in their favour and no consideration money was received by him from the said two persons. It was also the case of the plaintiff that the deeds of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui are forged and the plaintiff was never known as Sachindra Mohon Roy and the deeds standing in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were brought into existence by way of forgery and by the forged and fraudulent deeds no right, title and interest accrued to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad siddiqui, the vendors of the defendant Nos. I and 2, in the land in suit, that the defendants have trespassed into the 'B' schedule property and that 'S.A. Khatian was wrongly prepared in the name of Sachindra Mohon Roy.

4. The suit was contested by the appellants (defendant Nos.1 and 2) by filing written statement stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff is an Indian National and also fictitious person and is not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy @ Sachindra Mohon Roy, that Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui having not been impleaded in the suit the same is not maintainable, that the suit is barred by limitation, that said Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were in possession of the property in suit by purchase in 1969 from Jatindra Mohon Roy @ Sachindra Mohon Roy; that in the last part of 1972 defendant No.1 came to know that Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui; who were residing in the suit property, intending to sell the property in suit, the defendant No.1 agreed to purchase the same, that after their purchase when the defendants took possession of the property the defendant No.5 was in possession of a small portion of the suit property and he became a licensee under the defendants, that the defendants asked the said defendant No.5" to vacant the property but the having had refused the defendants instituted title suit. No. 449 of 1976 (subsequently numbered as title suit No. 429 of 1982) for eviction of the defendant No. 5, that the defendants after their purchase got their names mutated and paid rent and in the R.S. khatian their names have been duly recorded, that Chinta Haran Roy, who is prosecuting the suit on the basis of the Power of Attorney granted by the plaintiff and the defendant No.5, for the purpose of grabbing the property in suit has created false and fabricated Power of Attorney, that Sachindra Mohon Roy alias Jatindra Mohon Roy after transferring the property in question to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui left for India and died in Calcutta.

5. It was the consistent case of the contesting defendants that the suit has been filed by the attorney upon obtaining Power of Attorney from a fictitious person who has figured as plaintiff and that plaintiff is not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy @ Sachindra Mohon Roy who was the owner of the property of 62, Bama Charan Chakraborty Road (BCC Road) and who sold the same to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui, the vendors of the contesting defendants and the plaintiff who is claiming himself to be Jatindra Mohon Roy is not the person who executed the sale deeds Nos.16157 and 16158 dated October 27, 1969 in favour of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui.

6. It may be mentioned initially the suit was file seeking the reliefs (a) and (b) as mentioned above stating in paragraph 13 of the plaint "That the cause of action fo4 the suit arose on 27-10-69 at Bama Charan Chakraborty, Roy, P.S. Sutrapur within the Jurisdiction of this Court" meaning 1st Court of Subordinate Judge (now Court of Joint District Judge), Dhaka.

7. The Court of first instance decreed the suit on the findings that the suit framed was maintainable and was properly valued, that the attorney can very much prosecute the suit on the basis of Power of Attorney, that. Jatindra Mohon Roy, owner of the property in suit did not execute the deed Nos.16157 and 16158 on October 27, 1969 in favour of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohaminad Siddiqui and as such they had no capacity to transfer the property in suit to defendant Nos. 1 and 2, that possession of defendant Nos. I and 2 in the land in suit is illegal, that as the suit has been filed by Jatindra Mohon Roy the owner of the property through the constituted attorney Chinta Haran Roy as such question of locus standi to proceed with the suit is not entertain able, that the suit is not barred by limitation in the context of the provision of Section 18 of the Limitation Act.

8. The contesting defendants went on appeal. The appellate Court dismissed the suit upon reversing the judgment and decree of the trial Court on the findings that plaintiff did not establish by reliable evidence that the deeds in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqi were forged and fabricated and the plaintiff has also not established that the defendants were the trespassers in a portion of the land in suit, that the defendants have established that they on the basis of their purchase from Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wall Mohammad Siddiqui are in possession of the land.

9. The plaintiff moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division set aside the judgment and decree of the appellate Court upon observing "The learned Additional District Judge having failed to assess the evidence in its true perspective has caused failure of justice and the judgment of the learned Additional District Judge in that view of the matter cannot be sustained in law. The learned trial Court has elaborately discussed the documentary evidence and also taken notice of the oral, evidence adduced by the parties and conclusion followed that the plaintiffs (sic) have been able to prove their claim as regards the suit property and that the defendant Nos.1 and. 2 had not acquired any good title because their vendors documents of title were on the evidence found to be forged and fabricated". The High Court Division also held that the suit was not barred by limitation. It has further been observed by the High Court Division "It is further to be noted since the possession of the licence of the plaintiff has been established the proposition that the suit was not brought within 6 years from the date of cause of action as shown in the plaint and that the suit is barred by limitation cannot be accepted, Further it is stated that the date as has been given in paragraph 13 cannot be called the cause of action in its legal sense because cause of action is the bundle of facts as stated in the plaint. Having regard to the pleadings and the evidence the suit was filed within time as has been found by the trial Court and it is not barred by limitation". The High Court Division further held that defendants were not competent to take the plea of defect of party since they failed to give the particulars of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui reply to the interrogatories filed by the plaintiff. The High Court Division lastly held that defendants claim of right, title and interest in the property in suit cannot be accepted since they derived their alleged title from the persons whose acquisition of title in the property in suit by Ext. 9 and 9 (ka) (kabalas dated 27.10.1969) were found to be forged and fabricated.

10. Leave was granted to consider the contentions that it being the definite case of the appellants that Jatindra Mohon Roy, who was dead long back, and the doner of Power of Attorney in suit (Jatindra Mohon Roy) is not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy @ Sachindra Mohon Roy and he is a fictitious person and the prime issue was the identity of the person who claimed in the suit to be Jatindra Mahon Roy the trial Court and the High court Division were wrong in not dealing with and deciding the issue before decreeing the suit, that the statement in the pleadings being that the alleged plaintiff left the suit property in 1968 and that the cause of action according to the plaint having arisen on October 27, 1969 and. the suit having been filed on September 3, 1976 and the amendment of the plaint for inclusion of prayer (b)(I) and schedule 'C' having been done on July 10, 1988 (although admittedly in paragraph 9 of the plaint the plaintiff came to know about the deeds at the time of filing of the suit), the suit was clearly and hopelessly barred by limitation, that the suit so far as it concerns the validity of the kabalas dated October 27, 1969 is bad for defect of parties for not impleading the recipients of the said, kabalas and the High Court Division was wrong in decreeing the suit, that the High Court Division failed to take into consideration that the Power of Attorney of the Indian citizen (Jatindra Mohon Roy) was not duly authenticated by any Bangladesh authority, that the earlier orders of the High Court Division and the Appellate Division being with regard to the interlocutory matters the same cannot have sustaining effect on final decree.

11. It may be mentioned at the time of the hearing of the appeal from amongst the aforementioned contentions the learned Counsel for the appellants primarily made submission on the question of identity of the plaintiff as well as on the question of limitation. It was the consistent case of the defendants that the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is a fictitious person and not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy @ Sachindra Mohon Roy who was the owner of the property at 62 BCC Road and transferred the said property to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui.

12. Plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy did not depose in the suit although while the suit was ripen for hearing application was filed for taking down the deposition of plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy, who visited Bangladesh on Indian Passport, on commission but in the face of objection by the defendants the said prayer was rejected. It may also be mentioned an application was filed from plaintiff’s side for examination of the thumb impression of plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy with the thumb impression appearing in the deed of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui by Finger Print Expert. The prayer so made was opposed, by the contesting defendants raising question of identity of the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy being not the person who executed the deed in favour of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui. The prayer for examination of thumb impression was rejected on August 23, 1978:

13. From the plaintiff-Respondent's side it was contended that the contentions which are now being made in the appeal being questions of fact and having already been concluded by the findings and decisions made by the Court of first instance and the High Court Division the appellants are not in law competent to re-agitate the said questions in support of the appeal. In repelling this contention the learned Counsel for the appellants submitted that the questions, particularly question of identity of plaintiff, that ought to have been decided by the Court of first instance or by the courts below as those were specifically raised and in such a situation the failure so had happened On the part of the courts below becomes a question of law and this Court, hearing the appeal, is very much competent to see or examine whether there has been failure of duty imposed by law and in this connection he has referred to the case of Sheikh Rahmat Ilahi Vs. Mohammad Hayat Khan and others reported in AIR 1943 PC, 208 wherein it has been observed, "that where the Courts below had misconceived the real question of fact they had to try. There was an error of law on which a second appeal lay and their Lordships can see no difference in principle between a failure to appreciate and determine the real question of fact to be tried and a failure to appreciate and determine a question of fact which vitally affects the issue stated in the case. In either case the failure is a failure in the duty imposed by law upon the Court and the question whether there has been such a failure must in their Lordships' opinion is a question of law".

14. In support of the case that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned the property in suit the attorney Chinta Haran Roy examined himself as P.W.1 and to corroborate him P.Ws.2 and 3 have been examined. P.W.1 has deposed that property at 62 BCC Road was owned by Haridas Karmaker who died leaving son Krishna Chandra Karmaker and he died leaving son Jatindra Mohon Roy and Jatindra Mohon Roy mutated his name in Dhaka Municipality. In cross-examination witness has stated that Sachindra Mohon Roy @ Jatindra Mohon Roy was the owner of the property in suit. P.W.2 has stated that Jatindra Mohon Roy used to live in 61/1 B.C.C. Road which is 20/25 yards south of the property in suit. In cross-examination this witness has stated that Jatindra Mohon Roy was the owner of the house at 61/1 BCC Road. P.W.3 has stated that Jatindra Mohon Roy was the owner of the property in suit and Jatindra Mohon Roy used to live in 61 BCC Road south of the property at 62 BCC Road. In cross-examination the witness has stated that he has not seen any paper relating to the property in suit and Jatindra used to live opposite to the property in suit. The witness has further stated that Jatindra lived in 61 BCC Road and in 62 BCC Road Radha, his mother and others used to live, Jatindra used to visit the property in suit. This witness has categorically stated "জোতিন্দ্র মোহন নালিশী বাড়ীর মালিক ছিলেন কিনা জানি না" The above is the evidence from the side of the plaintiff as to identity of Jatindra Mohon Roy as well as to the ownership of the property in suit.

15. From the defendants side D.Ws.2 and 3, in support of the case that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned and possessed the property at 62 BCC Road and transferred the same to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui have deposed that Sachindra was the owner of the property in suit. In cross-examination D.W.2 has stated Sachindra used to stay in 62 BCC Road. D.W.3 has stated that prior to Ali Ahmed and others Sachindra was the owner of the property in suit. This witness has further stated that one Jatindra who used to live at 61/2 BCC Road was known to him and said Jatindra had never stayed in the property in suit. The witness has further stated that since 1969 Ali Ahmed had been staying in the property in suit and in 1969 Sachindra went to India and that if seen he would be able to recognize Sachindra. The witness has denied the suggestion that in the property in suit Jatindra Mohon Roy used to live and in the property in suit no person by name Jatindra used to live.

16. On consideration of the evidence brought on record from the plaintiffs side it is seen that the definite contention of the defendants that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is a fictitious person and that he was not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned and possessed the property of 62 BCC Road and sold the same to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui at all has not been dislodged. In the absence of establishing the identity of the plaintiff or in other words disproving the contention of the defendants that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned and possessed the property at 62 BCC Road the plaintiff was not entitled to any relief as prayed for and as such the trial Court as well as the High Court Division was in error in decreeing the suit in favour of the plaintiff in the absence of establishing the identity of the plaintiff. It may be mentioned from the evidence brought on record from the plaintiffs side it is seen that Jatindra Mohon Roy in whose name the suit has been filed was the owner of the property at 61 or 61/1 BCC Road and was not the owner of the property at 62 BCC Road.

17. The learned Counsel for the plaintiff; Respondent in supporting the judgment of the trial Court and the High Court Division as to identity of the plaintiff has submitted that the defendants in their written statement in paragraphs 8 and 11 admitted correctness of the statements made in paragraph Nos.l-3 and 6 of the plaint. The statements made in the aforesaid paragraph Nos.1-3 of the plaint are as to devolution of the property described in schedule 'A' to the plaint and of taking steps by the claimant of the property as to mutation of his name in the revenue record and municipal record and the statements made in paragraph 6 of the plaint are as to situation in the background whereof the plaintiff left the area where the property situates. But upon reading the statements made in the written statement it is seen that specific case of the contesting defendants is that the suit has been filed by using the name of one fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy and upon obtaining Power of Attorney from the said fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy. In the aforesaid background of the case of the respective parties it was for the plaintiff to establish that the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is not a fictitious person, rather the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy was the person who owned the property in suit, but unfortunately the plaintiff has not deposed in support of his case and in rebuttal of defendants specific case that plaintiff Jatindra Mahon Roy is a fictitious one and not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned the property in suit and transferred to defendants' vendors has not examined the plaintiff inspite of being present in Bangladesh at a time when the suit was ready for hearing and avoided his examination in Court by resorting to the prayer for taking clown evidence on commission.

18. The learned Counsel for the appellants has submitted that when the defendants challenged identity. of the plaintiff and the genuineness of the Power of Attorney obtained from Jatindra Mahon Roy it was for the plaintiff to establish that the plaintiff Jatindra Mahon 'Roy is not a fictitious person rather the owner of the property in suit and that the Power of Attorney is not from a fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy. It may be mentioned it was the case of the defendants that the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is not the Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned the property at 62 BCC Road and from whom Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui purchased the property. The learned Counsel for the plaintiff Respondent upon referring to the passport of Jatindra Mohon Roy (Ext.14) and the entries therein including the Visa and the endorsement showing Jatindra Mohon Roy's leaving Bangladesh has submitted that from the defendants' side there was no challenge as to the genuineness of the passport and the entries therein. It may be mentioned Jatindra Mahan Roy visited Bangladesh on the basis of a passport issued by the Government of India on July 26, 1978 and upon referring to the Ext.14 and the entries therein the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-Respondent has submitted that genuineness of the plaintiff Jatindra Mahon Roy was sufficiently established by the entries in Ext.14. Suffice it to say the passport and the entries therein are no doubt relate to the holder of said pass-port and even if for argument's sake it is accepted that said Jatindra Mohon Roy as plaintiff filed the suit but the fact is that it was not established by reliable evidence that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy in the face of challenge from the side of the defence that the suit has been filed by the fictitious person is the real Jatindra Mohon Roy, who was the owner of the property at 62 BCC Road. The learned Counsel of the plaintiff- Respondent as. against the contention of defendants as to non-establishing of identity of plaintiff submitted that in the background of the case of the defense that suit has been filed by fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy and not by the real Jatindra Mohon Roy, who sold his property to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui, it was the duty of the defendants to take steps for production of plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy who visited Bangladesh on the basis of Ext.14 before the Court and in this connection the learned Counsel has referred to the proviso to Rule 1 of Order 3 and order 5 Rule 3 (2) of the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC). The submission so made appears to be not well founded in law since provision in the proviso to Order 3 Rule 1 relates to compliance of order of the Court by any party for ' appearance in person and the other provision of Order 5 Rule 3(2) CPC relates to compliance of the order of the Court directing the plaintiff to appear in person before the Court on specified date. As per provision of law referred to above it is the Court that may require a party itself to appear before the Court. In the background of the challenge made as to the identity of the plaintiff it was the duty of the plaintiff to establish the fact that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy was the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned the property at 62 BCC Road. Person who visited Bangladesh on the basis of Ext.14 was present in Bangladesh when the suit was ready for hearing. The plaintiff instead of taking steps for taking down his evidence in Court who visited the Court premises filed petition seeking permission for taking down his evidence on commission. The application so filed was contested by the defendants stating specifically that Jatindra Mohon Roy who figured as plaintiff was a fictitious person. In the afore state of the matter the plaintiff was required to establish the plaintiff was Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned the property in suit, but did not establish the same.

19. The learned Counsel for the appellants has submitted that Court has always deprecated the conduct of a litigant who is present in Court but did not go into the witness box and is not examined as a witness of his own inspite of being an essential witness and to force the other party to call him and so suffer the discomfiture of having him treated as his, (the other party's) own witness and in this connection has referred to the case of Sardar Gurbakhsh Singh Vs. Gurdial Singh and another reported in AIR 1927, PC. 230 wherein it has been observed "This is thought to be clever, but it is a bad and degrading practice" and "a vicious practice, unworthy of a high-toned or reputable system of advocacy".

20. The learned Counsel of the plaintiff-Respondent in support of the contention that the identity of the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy was established by the evidence on record has referred to the evidence of P. Ws. and D.W.3. P.W.I has stated that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy who died on January 17, 1987 was his father in law and he gave him Power of Attorney to file and prosecute the suit and after plaintiffs death his heirs (5 sons) have been substituted and they have given him Power of Attorney (Ext.2) that Jatindra Mohon Roy mutated his name in respect of the property bearing holding No.62 BCC Road, that Jatindra Mohon Indian passport has been filed in Court and in the passport (Ext.14) there are signatures and the photo of Jatindra Mohon Roy. The evidence of P.Ws.2 and 3 has been noted hereinbefore. The learned Counsel has also referred to the statement of D.W.3 in cross-examination wherein he has identified the photo in the passport as of Jatindra and stated that Jatindra had no other name. This witness has also stated that it was not known to him whether name of Jatindra was Jatindra Mohon Roy and Jatindra was known to him and he was well educated man and he used to serve in the Bangladesh Bank, branch at, Sadar Ghat and it is not true that in the property in suit Jatindra Mohon Roy used to stay and in the said property none by name Sachindra used to live. The evidence so retie upon from plaintiff-Respondent's side in our view in no way has established the fact that plaints Jatindra Mohan Roy was the owner of the property at 62 BCC Road or in other words has dislodged the challenge of the defendants that plaintiff is a fictitious person and that he was not the owner of the property at 62 BCC Road, nor the plaintiff is the Jatindra Mohon Roy who sold the property at 62 BCC Road to All Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui.

<u>21. The learned Counsel for the plaintiff-Respondent upon referring to the signature of Jatindra Mohon Roy in Ext.14 and in the background of the evidence of D.W, 3 that Jatindra Babu was a well educated man submitted that these very evidence clearly established that the signatures appearing in the kabalas (Exts.9 and 9 ka) dated 27.10.1969 were not of the plaintiff since Jatindra Mohon Roy who was a well educated man would not have signed his name in the manner as appears in the kabalas and thus it is sufficiently clear that the kabalas (Exts.9 and 9 Ka) were not genuine or in other words were not executed by plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy. In the absence of establishing the identity of plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Ray upon referring to the signatures appearing in the passport (Ext.14) it cannot be said that the signatures appearing in the kabalas dated 27.10.1969 were not of Jatindra Mohan Roy who transferred the property at 62 BCC Road to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui. By the evidence produced by the plaintiff and also the evidence relied upon by him, as discussed above, it has neither been established the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy was the Jatindra Mohon Roy alias Sachindra Mohon Roy who owned property at 62 BCC Road, nor it has been established that plaintiff was the owner of the property in suit.</u>

22. The learned Counsel for the plaintiff-Respondent in summing up his submissions submitted that contention of the defendants as to non-establishing the identity of the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy merits no consideration as defendants did not take any step to prove their case that plaintiff Jatindra Mohan Roy was a fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy and not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who sold the property at 62 BCC Road to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui, that defendants have admitted ownership of the property at 62 BCC Road by Jatindra Mohon Roy, that the defendants have not taken step to prove their case that suit was filed by fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy and that Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui purchased the property from Jatindra Mohon Roy who was the owner of the property at 62 BCC Road, that defendants did not take any step for producing plaintiff-Jatindra Mohon Roy in Court and did not press the petition filed with the prayer for making direction to the plaintiff to examine plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy's son and that no step was taken by the defendants to establish that Power of Attorney was executed by fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy. Suffice it to say that it was the duty of the plaintiff to establish that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy was the genuine Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned the property at 62 BCC Road and only thereafter it was the duty of the defendants to establish their case that the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy was a fictitious person and the suit was not filed by real Jatindra Mohon Roy who owned the property at 62 BCC Road and sold the said property to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui from whom the defendants purchased the property in suit. The other contentions are of no merit because of the established rule that at first plaintiff is to prove his case and then onus shifts upon the defendants to establish his contention or to disprove plaintiffs case.

<u>23. The plaintiff has filed the suit seeking the reliefs as stated hereinbefore. One of the relief was for declaration of title. It is the definite case of the plaintiff that cause of action of the suit arose on 27th October, 1969. The, suit was filed on September 3, 1976. Thereafter on July 10, 1988 plaintiff filed petition seeking amendment of the plaint by inserting some facts as well as an additional relief i.e. b (1) seeking declaration that the deeds bearing Nos.16157 and 16158 dated 27.10.1969 showing transfer of the property at 62 BCC Road to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui by Jatindra Mohon Roy alias Sachindra Mohon Roy is forged, fabricated and that the transfers by the said Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui, to the defendant Nos.1 and 2 are illegal and not binding on the plaintiff. This prayer for amendment was allowed on November 19, 1988.</u>

24. In the background of the pleadings of the parties and issue as to limitation so framed it was contended on behalf of the defendants that plaintiff having had asserted that cause of action arose on October 27, 1969, the reliefs sought as to declaration of title and the declaration as regard the deeds dated October 27, 1969 (Exts.9 and 9 'Ka') were barred by limitation since the suit was not filed within 6 years in the background of the provision of section 120 of the Limitation Act.

25. In refuting the contention of the defendants it was submitted from the side of the plaintiff that their case is covered by the provision of section 18 of the Limitation Act.

26. The Court of first instance disposed of the question of limitation in favour of the plaintiff in holding that in the background of the facts and in view of the provision of law the suit is not barred by limitation. The trial Court relied upon section 18 of the Limitation Act. The appellate Court disposed of the question of limitation in the affirmative upon observing as the cause of action arose on 27th October, 1969 as such the suit filed on September 3, 1976 was barred.

27. The High Court Division was of the view that defendants occupied the 'Kha' schedule property in the year 1975 by forte and the rest of the property was under the possession of the licensee of the plaintiff who was later on evicted by the proceeding initiated by the defendants without impleading the plaintiff and then upon observing "Considering all these it can unhesitatingly be said that the suit was brought within time and it is not barred by limitation. It is further to be noted since the possession of the licensee of the plaintiff has been established the proposition that the suit was not brought within 6 years from the date of cause of action as shown in the plaint and that the suit is barred by limitation cannot be accepted. Further it is stated that the date as has been given in paragraph 13 cannot be called the cause of action in its legal sense because action is the bundle of facts as stated in the plaint. Having regard to the pleadings and the evidence the suit was filed within time as has been found by the trial Court and it is not barred by limitation".

28. The suit was filed on September 3, 1976 making specific statement that the cause of action for the same arose on October 27, 1969. The date so given is the date on which Jatindra Mohon Roy alias Sachindra Mohon Roy transferred the property in suit to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui. The reliefs sought were in all three and of those two were of declaratory nature and the 3rd was for recovery of possession of the property described in schedule 'B' which is part of the property described in schedule 'A' to the plaint. The relief as to recovery of possession of the property described in schedule 'B' was sought upon averring that plaintiff was dispossessed by the defendant Nos.1 and 2 sometime in 1975.

29. It is apparent in the context of the averments made in the plaint that the cause of action arose on October 27, 1969, the reliefs sought of the declaratory nature were barred since the suit was filed on 3ra September, 1976. The trial Court disposed of the question of limitation as regard the reliefs which were of declaratory nature upon referring to the provision of section 18 of the Limitation Act and the High Court Division disposed of the question of limitation upon referring to the case of the plaintiff that he was dispossessed in 1975 of a part of the, property in suit and the rest of the property was in the possession of plaintiffs licensee but the defendants upon initiating a proceeding without impleading the plaintiff evicted his licensee and upon observing the date "given in paragraph 13 cannot be called the cause of action in its legal sense because action is the bundle of facts as stated in the plaint".

30. It may be mentioned in the background of the provisions of law as in Order 6 Rule 4 and Order 7 Rule 6 of the Code of Civil Procedure there is total absence of averment making out a case to have the aid of the provision of section 18 of the Limitation Act for the purpose of taking out of the reliefs (a) and (b) (1) case froth the clutch of the limitation. Matters in respect whereof relief (b) (1), which was inserted by the amendment allowed on November 19, 1988, were very much known to the plaintiff at the time of filing the suit. It was the contention of the appellants that the relief (a) was barred by limitation because of categorical statement in the plaint that the cause of filing the suit arose on October 27, 1969 i.e. the date on which Jatindra Mohon Roy alias Sachindra Mohon Roy transferred the property in suit to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui. It was also the contention of the appellants that the fact of transfer of the property in suit by the deeds dated October 27,1969 (Exts.9 and 9 'ka') in respect whereof relief (b) (1) was sought by filing an application for amendment on July 10, 1988 and was allowed on November 19, 1988 was totally barred since the said matter even if not earlier, but at least was known on the date of filing the suit.

<u>31. The plaintiff has prayed for declaration of title stating that his cause for seeking such relief arose on October 27, 1969. As stated earlier the suit was filed on September 3, 1976. In the background .of the aforesaid fact the relief so sought was barred in view of the provision of Article 120 of the Limitation Act. The other relief i.e. relief b(I) was also barred under Article 120 of the Limitation Act in the background of the fact stated hereinbefore. It may be mentioned that the relief's (a) and (b) i.e. declaration of title in respect of the property in schedule 'A' and recovery of khas possession of the property described in schedule 'B' are independent reliefs and as such in case the relief as regard declaration of title if is found to be barred then there is no question of granting relief as to recovery of possession of the property (in 'B' schedule) which is part of the property in respect whereof declaration of title has been sought. It has been submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellants that plaintiff has elected for the relief as in prayer (b)(I) since in the absence thereof he cannot have the complete relief in the suit and as such keeping the said aspect of the matter in view he proceeded with the suit seeking relief in respect of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 (Exts.9 and 9 'ka'). The relief's so sought as has already been found are barred since no case was made out in the pleading nor evidence was led to claim exemption from law of limitation. In reply to the submission of the appellants' learned Counsel on the point of limitation as regard the relief as in (b) (I) i.e. declaration in respect of the deeds dated 27.10.1969 (Exts. 9 and 9 'ka') it has been submitted by the learned Counsel of the plaintiff-Respondent that said relief was redundant as without seeking the said relief the suit could be proceeded and could have the relief's sought in prayer (a) and (b) since in making decision as to the relief's (a) and (b) the documents dated 27.10.1969 (Exts.9 and 9 'ka') would have been an issue and as such plaintiffs suit is not liable to be dismissed or in other words plaintiff cannot be disentitled to have the reliefs as in prayer (a) and (b) i.e. declaration of title and recovery of khas possession. It has also been submitted by the learned Counsel for the plaintiff Respondent that the cause of action as has been stated in the plaint is in no way related to the plaintiffs case of dispossession and that the same at best be referred to the two documents as regard which relief has been sought in prayer (b)(I). The learned Counsel continued that plaintiff has stated his case of dispossession from the 'B' schedule land in paragraphs 6 and 7 of the plaint. It may be mentioned in paragraph 6 of the plaint it has been stated that plaintiff left the area where the property situates in 1968 when law and order situation deteriorated there and in paragraph 7 it has been stated that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are occupying portion of the property in suit described in schedule 'B' since after liberation of the country. It may be mentioned no specific date of dispossession has been stated in the plaint. The learned Counsel upon referring to the averments made in paragraphs 6 and 7 of the plaint has submitted that as in the absence of relief (b) (I) the suit could be proceeded and that the relief as to recovery of possession as is not barred by limitation and consequently as the suit is not liable to fail on the ground of limitation the trial Court as well as the High Court Division had correctly held that the suit was not barred by limitation. It may be mentioned relief sought for declaration of title upon making the averment that the cause of action for filing the suit arose on October 27; 1969 was certainly barred by limitation since suit was filed on September 3, 1976. The learned Counsel for, the plaintiff-Respondent tried to take out the suit from the precincts of limitation upon referring to the provision of Article 4 of the Bangladesh (Legal Proceedings) Order, 1972 (President's Order No.12 of 1972). The provision of Article 4 reads as:</u>

<u>"4: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for time being in force, in computing the period of limitation prescribed for any legal proceeding by or under any law, the period between the 1st day of March, 1971 and the 1st day of March, 1972 (both days inclusive), shall be excluded".</u>

32. Reliance so placed upon the provision of Article 4 of P.0.12 of 1972 for having the suit out of the ambit of limitation appears to be not well founded if considered in the context of the object and the purpose for which the said law was enacted.

33. In the preamble of P.0.12 of 1972 it has been stated that during the material period . i.e. 1g of March, 1971 and 1g day of March, 1972 there was disruption of normal life and activities throughout Bangladesh and that because of the situation created by the occupation army people were not able to go to Courts or Tribunals to institute legal proceedings and as a result many claims and legal rights have become time-barred" and as such for the ends of justice, it is necessary to provide for the saving of limitation for all legal proceedings. So It is seen that in the background of the aforesaid state of the matter President's Order No.12 of 1972 was promulgated. to provide for saving of limitation in respect of the proceeding which were required to be file between the 1g day of March, 1971 and 1g day of March, 1972 and that because of the condition that was prevalent at the mentioned period the proceeding could not initiated and thus became barred by limitation. The proceeding that was initiated by the plaintiff was not of the kind as contemplated by the provision of President's Order No.12 of 1972 i.e. plaintiffs suit was not a one which because of the prevailing condition during the period between 1st  day of March, 1971 and the day of March, 1972 become barred by limitation. In that view of the matter aid as has been sought for upon resorting to Article 4 of President's Order No.12 of 1972 for taking the suit out of the clutch of limitation is not available to the plaintiff and consequently his relief as in (a) was barred by limitation. . The relief seeking declaration of title being barred by-limitation the other reliefs were not available to the plaintiff. The High Court Division as well as the trial Court while disposing of the question of limitation were in serious error in that High Court Division proceeded on the premises that the relief as to recovery of possession was not barred by limitation and the other portion of the property in suit, as to which recovery of possession was prayed for was in the possession of the lisencee of the plaintiff who was illegally evicted by the defendants upon initiating proceeding without impleading the plaintiff and that date given in paragraph 13 of the plaint cannot be Called the cause of action and the trial Court decided the question of limitation in favour of the plaintiff upon referring to the provision of section 18 of the Limitation Act although no case was made out for recording to the said provision of law. The averment as to cause of action is definite and there" is no material in the plaint to conclude that cause of action averred is not the one but there is or are some other date or period of cause of action.

34. The other ground on which leave obtained was that the suit as the same it concerned to- the validity of the kabalas dated October 27, 1969 was bad for defect of parties for not impleading the recipients of the said kabalas and as such the High Court Division was wrong in decreeing the suit.

35. The plaintiff, whose identity was seriously challenged, filed the suit seeking declaration of title in respect of the property in suit and for khas possession of the part of the suit property described in schedule 'B' attached to the plaint. The suit was filed on September 3, 1976. On July 10, 1988 the plaintiff filed an application seeking amendment of the plaint by way of insertion of some facts and the relief (b)(I) i.e. seeking declaration that the kabalas (Exts.9 and 9 `ka') dated October 27, 1969 in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were forged, fraudulent and" not binding upon the plaintiff. Although aforesaid declaration was sought but the recipients of the said kabalas i.e. Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were not impleaded in the suit. In that state of the matter it was the consistent contention of the appellants that the suit was bad for defect of parties for non-impleading the said 2 (two) persons. It may be mentioned that appellants while filed the written statement in February 1977 averred that the suit was bad for defect of party for non-impleading the Government of Bangladesh as well as Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui, the vendors of the contesting defendants. The plaintiff added the Government of Bangladesh in the category of defendants. It appears from the record of the suit that interrogatory was served on the defendants to furnish address of the persons who were not made party in the suit and defendants having not replied thereto the plaintiff filed an application with the prayer for debarring them from raising the plea of defect of party and the Court allowed the said prayer. The plaintiff filed an application seeking amendment of the plaint on July 10, 1988. The Court by the order dated November 19, 1988 allowed the prayer for amendment of the plaint and thereupon, amongst others, additional relief (b)(I) was inserted in the plaint seeking declaration that the deeds of 27th October, 1969 in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff. On the incorporation of relief (b) (I) the suit under went transformation making it obligatory for plaintiff, to implead the recipients of Exts.9 and 9 (ka) since those vendees became necessary parties and in their absence no legally sustainable decree be passed against them. On the incorporation of relief (b) (I) as the suit assumed the character different from pre-amendment the order debarring defendants from raising plea of defect of party passed prior to the amendment of plaint incorporating relief (b) (I) lost its force since with the amendment of plaint the vendees of Exts.9 and 9 (ka) who prior to amendment were neither necessary nor proper party, became necessary party and their particulars were very much available in Exts:9 and 9 (ka).

36. At all level the contesting defendants contended that the suit so far the same relates to (b) (I) i.e. seeking declaration that the deeds dated October 27, 1969 are forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff was bad for defect of party for non-Impleading the recipients of the said deeds. The admitted possession is that the recipients of the deeds of October 27, 1969 were not made party in the suit although relief was sought in respect of the said deeds.

37. The trial Court has not disposed of the contention of the defendants as regard defect of party for non-impleading the recipients of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 because of seeking declaration that the said deeds were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff.

38. The High Court Division has disposed of the appellants' contention as to defect of parties for non-impleading the recipients of the kabalas dated October 27, 1969 upon observing that the defendant-appellants. were debarred from raising the question of non joinder of parties by the order dated 15.7.1986. It may be mentioned High Court Division was quite unmindful of the fact that relief (b)(I) i.e. declaration sought for that the deeds of October 27, 1969 were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff Was inserted in the plaint in pursuant to the order dated November 19, 1988 allowing the petition dated July 10, 1988 seeking amendment of the plaint.

<u>39. The plaintiff filed the suit on September 3, 1976 keeping in view the deeds dated October 27, 1969 and that later on got inserted the relief (b)(I) since in the absence of declaration as in relief (b)(1), the reliefs i.e. declaration of title and recovery of possession if allowed would not be a complete one. The undisputed position in law is that plaintiff cannot have a relief against a person who is not a party in the suit. In the instant case deeds of October 27, 1969 in respect of whereof relief has been sought by way of declaration that the said deeds were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff were in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui or in other words the said two persons were the recipients of the deeds of October 27, 1969. Although relief sought in respect of the deeds of October 27, 1969 but the recipients of the same were not made party in the suit. The High Court Division was not correct in rejecting the contention of the defendants, that the suit so far the same relates to deeds of October 27, 1969 was bad for defect of party for non impleading the recipients of the said deeds as because the Court by the order dated July 15, 1986 debarred the defendants from taking the plea of defect of party in a different context and at a time when relief seeking declaration that the deeds of October 27, 1969 were forged and fraudulent were not the subject matter of the suit.</u>

40. The learned Counsel for the plaintiff-Respondent has submitted that the defendants in their written statement filed in 1977 mentioned the names of the persons who were not made parties in the suit and thereupon plaintiff impleaded one of those and served interrogatory as regard the others but the defendants did not reply to the interrogatory and thereupon the Court made order debarring defendants from raising the plea that the suit is bad for defect of party. The learned Counsel also submitted that recipients of the deeds of October 27, 1969 (Exts.9 and 9 (ka)) were not necessary and proper party in the suit since they have transferred their interest to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and as such challenge to the validity of the deeds on the basis whereof defendant Nos. and 2 raised claim in the land in suit was in effect challenge to the document recipients whereof were Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui. The learned Counsel continued that determination of the validity or legality of documents on which defendants based their claim in the land in suit as well as the documents on the basis of which defendants' documents were made is germane in the background of the reliefs sought by way of declaration of title and recovery of possession. It was further submitted by the learned Counsel that because of the provision of Order 1, Rule 10 (2) read with order 22 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure for non-impleading of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui the suit cannot be said bad for defect of party. It has lastly been submitted by the learned Counsel that defendant Nos. 1 and 2 being the claimant of the land in suit were required to answer the issue raised in the suit since the recipients of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 divested their interest by selling the property of the said deeds to the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and as such recipients of the deeds of October 27, 1969 were neither necessary nor proper party in the suit.

<u>41. Provision of Order 22, Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides for continuation of a suit in the background of the situation given therein i.e. assignment, creation or devolution of any interest during the pendency of the suit. In the instant case none of the aforesaid situations are present and as such the said provision is of no assistance to the plaintiff-Respondent in rebutting the contention of the appellants that the suit so far the same relates to validity of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 for non-impleading the recipients of the said deeds is bad in law. The other contention that because of the provision of Order 1, Rule 10(2) the suit cannot be said bad for defect of party for non-impleading the recipients of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 is also not legally well founded since it was incumbent upon the plaintiff to implead the persons against whom, as in the instant case against the recipients of the deeds dated October 27, 1969, relief is sought. The contention that the recipients of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 were not necessary and proper party in the suit is also not legally sustainable since relief has been sought in respect of the documents recipients whereof were Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui and the suit was filed keeping in view the deeds of October 27, 1969 and as it appears plaintiff in November 1988 got the relief (b)(I), i.e. declaration that the deed of October 27, 1969 was forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff inserted in the pleading by amendment since the other relief s sought would not be complete in the absence of declaration in respect of the deeds of October 27, 1969. The other contention that challenge to the document of defendant Nos.1 and 2 was in effect challenge to the deeds dated October 27, 1969 and that reliefs by way of declaration of title and recovery of possession were germane in the determination of the documents on the basis whereof defendants raised claim in the land in suit is also not correct in that fact in the background whereof deeds of October 27, 1969 were made were known to the recipients of those and they were the competent persons to explain the situation in the background whereof they obtained the document from Jatindra Mohon Roy @ Sachindra Mohon Roy. Moreover plaintiff has sought relief against the deeds of October 27, 1969 recipients whereof Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui and as such they were very much required to be made parties in the suit since relief was sought against the documents whereby they acquired title in the land in suit.</u>

42. The plaintiff after lapse of more than 12 years since the date of institution of the suit by way of amendment sought the relief (b)(I)i.e. declaration that the deeds of October 27, 1969 in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff and thus relief having in fact sought against the recipients of the deeds of October 27, 1969 (Ext.9 and 9 (ka) the said recipients became necessary party in the suit and a such plaintiff was required to implead them in the suit and that having not impleaded them the suit so far the same related to it the validity of the deeds of October 27, 1969 was bad for defect of party since they were necessary parties in presence of whom the relief sought in respect of the deeds of October 27, 1969 were required to be adjudicated. In this connection reference may be made to the decision in the case of Mt. Jahan Ara Begum Vs. Al. Md. Shamsul Hoque reported in 27 DLR (AD) 129 wherein it has been held "The position in law undoubtedly is that in the absence of a necessary party a decree cannot be made in favour of the plaintiff. Of course, the question as to what parties are necessary is often not easy to determine. One test which has been recognized as of great importance is that when in the absence of a party the court cannot give an effective remedy, that party is a necessary party. Besides, in order that a party may be considered a necessary party two conditions must be satisfied, first, that there must be a right to some relief against him in respect of the matter involved in the suit and, second, that his presence should be necessary in order to enable the court effectively and completely to adjudicate upon and settle the question involved in the suit". The learned Counsel for the appellants in support of the contention that because of non-impleading the necessary party against whom the relief was sought by way of seeking declaration that the deeds of October 27, 1969 were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff and thus the recipients of the said deeds became necessary party and they having not been impleaded the suit so far the same relates to the relief (b) (I) was bad for defect of party has referred to the case of Mohar Ali and others Vs. Zafar Ali and others reported in 27 MR, 451 wherein it has been observed "On the question of non-joinder of parties reference may be made to the provisions of Order 1 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in which it has been laid down that no objection on the ground of non-joinder of parties shall be given effect to unless it has been taken at the earliest possible opportunity and when such objection has not been so taken, it shall be deemed to have been waived. This question, however, is subject to another legal principle. It is no doubt true that the party to a suit shall not be allowed to agitate the question of non-joinder or misjoinder of parties at a subsequent stage if such a plea has not been taken at the earliest opportunity. But there is also another principle which has received judicial recognition, according to which no court shall pass an in fructuous decree. If it is found on a consideration of the evidence on record that a necessary party has not been impleaded in consequence whereof the decree which may be passed in the suit may be set at naught at the instance of the non-impleaded person, such a decree shall not be passed by a Court".

43. As has already been mentioned the suit was filed keeping in view the deeds dated October 27, 1969 recipients whereof were Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui and it is apparent that the plaintiff having had realized that in the absence of a declaration as was sought for in relief (b) (I) the other reliefs prayed for in the suit even if granted would not be complete one and thus the plaintiff having had sought for relief against the recipients of the deeds dated October 27, 1969 the recipients thereof were required to be made party and having had not impleaded the recipients of the deeds of October 27, 1969 the suit was certainly bad for defect of party so far the same concerned with relief (b) (I) .

44. The trial Court held that by the deeds dated October 27, 1969 Jatindra Mahon Roy did not alienate his interest in the land in suit in favour of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui. It is seen from the judgment of the trial Court that in making the said finding the said Court placed reliance on the report of the Hand Writing Expert (Ext. 10). It may be mentioned Hand Writing Expert was not examined by the parties. In that view of the matter the trial Court was in serious error in making the judgment on the basis of the report of the Hand Writing Expert which was not admissible in evidence because of non-examination of the Expert who made the report. Moreover plaintiff’s identity was required to be established because of the definite case of the defendants that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy is a fictitious person and that he was not the real Jatindra Mahon Roy alias Sachindra Mohon Roy who transferred the property in suit to All Ahmed Khandker and Wall Mohammad Siddiqui. We have already held that plaintiff miserably failed to establish the identity of Jatindra Mohon Roy who figured as plaintiff and allegedly was the owner of the property at 62 BCC road and it was not the Jatindra Mohon Roy alias Sachindra Mohan Roy who transferred the property in suit to the recipients of the deeds dated October 27, 1969. Of course plaintiff is not competent to raise the last plea since he having no interest in the land in suit not competent. It is also seen from the judgment of the trial Court that the said Court resorted to the mode as provides in section 73 of the Evidence Act and thereupon comparing signature in the pass port (Ext.14) and in the Power of Attorney (Ext. 1 'ka') with the signature appearing in the deeds .of October 27, 1969 held the document of October 27, 1969 forged. The mode so resorted to by the trial Court was erroneous since identity of the plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy whose signature claimed to be in Ext. 14, and Ext. 1 (ka), was not established in the background of the contention of the defendants that the said plaintiff is a fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy and not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who transferred the property in suit by the deeds dated October 27, 1969 to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui. The High Court Division concurred with the finding and decision of the trial Court as regard the deeds dated October 27, 1969. Since the finding of the trial Court that by the deeds of October 27, 1969 plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy did not transfer the land in suit was arrived at on the basis of inadmissible evidence and upon resorting to a made whereof there was no basis, as such the said finding of the trial Court and the High Court Division was not legally sustainable.

45. It is pertinent to mention that the settled principle of law is that view expressed by the Court in disposing of interlocutory matter and in the appeals or revision arising out of the order passed in the interlocutory matter has no bearing on the final disposal of the matter in which interlocutory order or orders were passed. In the background of the said settled principle of law the observation(s) made by this Di vision and the High Court Division while disposing of the appeals or revision arising out of the interlocutory orders as to defect of party or identity of the plaintiff had no bearing on the final disposal of the matter in issue in the suit or in other words matters upon adjudication where of suit was required to be disposed. It was submitted by the learned Counsel for the plaintiff-respondent that although defendants raised ground in the memorandum of appeal as to identity of the plaintiff but ultimately abandoned the same and the learned Counsel has also submitted that the question of identity of the plaintiff was not noted in the appeal or in the revision and as such even if leave has been granted to consider the contention of the appellants’ as regard the identity of the plaintiff, the said contention merits no consideration. The submission that the plaintiff abandoned the ground raised in the appeal as to identity of the plaintiff is not well founded since the same is a mere guess because it was the consistent case of the appellants that plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy was a fictitious man and not the real Jatindra Mohon Roy who transferred the land in suit by the deeds of October 27, 1969 to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui, vendors of the defendant Nos. 1 and 2. As it appears that the Court(s) failed to appreciate and determine a vital question of fact i.e. identity of the plaintiff and having had failed' to decide the identity of the plaintiff it cannot be said that the leave obtained on the question of identity of the plaintiff deserves no consideration since on the determination of the vital fact i.e. identity of the plaintiff the suit could be maintained and proceeded with and finally decreed in favour of the plaintiff but that was not done by the trial Court as well as by the High Court Division.

46. The learned Counsel of the appellants in reply to the submission of the learned Counsel of the plaintiff Respondent as to identity of the plaintiff submitted that it was the definite case of the defendants that the person who executed the Power. of Attorney at the time of filing the suit was not the vendor of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui and that defendants in their written statement specifically denied the identity of the plaintiff and stated that the suit has been filed by the fictitious person other than Jatindra Mohon Roy alias Sachindra Mohon Roy who was the owner of the property at 62 BCC Road and transferred the same to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wall Mohammad Siddiqui and that P.W.2 has stated that the photo in Ext.14 is of Jatindra Mohon who used to live in 61/1 BCC Road and the same is 20/25 yards away from suit property and Jatindra was the owner of 61/1 BCC Road and D.W.3 has stated that he did not know plaintiff Jatindra Mohon Roy and that one Jatindra was known to him and he lived in 61/2 BCC Road and that since 1969 Ali Ahmed was staying in the suit property. In view of the evidence of D.W.3 his identification of the signature and the photo in Ext.14 did no way establish the identity of the plaintiff or in other words dislodged the contention of the defendants that the suit has been filed by a fictitious Jatindra Mohon Roy and not by the Jatindra Mahon Roy alias Sachindra Mohon Roy who sold the property to Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui.

47. In the background of our discussions made hereinabove we are of the view that the appeal has merit.

48. Accordingly the appeal is allowed. There is no order as to cost.

End.
